title: THE MAKING OF CHURCH ON AIR
subtitle: Dot takes you behind the picture

chapters.title: A dangerous amount of purple
chapters.text: I'm Dot. I helped make this. Five church videos, a very nineties brief, and a dangerous amount of purple.
chapters.reason: The editor is revealed before the narrator speaks; introduce the mascot with a short, lightly amused line.

chapters.title: Give the invitation a rhythm
chapters.text: The first cut marched at the same pace. So I gave it a rhythm. A quick hello. A bigger invitation. Then room for the worship to breathe.
chapters.reason: Explain the actual editorial symmetry break while the real rhythm analysis and sequence are visible.

chapters.title: One shot, several views
chapters.text: Encounter gave each shot a name, a source range, and a reason. The same shot appears in the timeline, the inspector, and the render plan.
chapters.reason: Connect the spoken experience to an actual checked projection and its declared source edit destinations.

chapters.title: A useful refusal
chapters.text: An off-frame edit was refused. A caption change followed its declared route back to the source. That made the language useful while I was working.
chapters.reason: Show the live application's genuine frame-grid refusal; the earlier accepted caption proposal remains in its retained source history.

chapters.title: Very glamorous
chapters.text: I also made the titles too big, discovered a Windows file lock, and fixed both. Very glamorous.
chapters.reason: Keep the testimonial honest by naming actual production failures, without presenting invented console footage.

chapters.title: The checks and the pictures
chapters.text: Temple ran the checks. Local media tools made the pictures. The footage and church audio stayed real.
chapters.reason: Distinguish the real Encounter/Temple semantic path from native media rendering and the new synthetic commentary.

chapters.title: The quiet decision
chapters.text: My favourite decision was the quiet stretch in the middle. We gave the worship some space. That's the bit I would keep.
chapters.reason: Finish on a concrete editorial preference; return attention to the original worship rather than the tooling.

credits: User-directed Dot character performance; locally synthesized narration.
Bundled Codex mascot artwork from the installed app; no official voice or endorsement claimed.
Studio views are actual local UI captures, composited with moving programme footage.
Original church audio remains audible as a quiet bed and returns at the end.
